1.sword: There is a plant seed on its back right from the day this Pokémon is born. The seed slowly grows larger.
1.shield: While it is young, it uses the nutrients that are stored in the seed on its back in order to grow.

2.sword: When the bulb on its back grows large, it appears to lose the ability to stand on its hind legs.
2.shield: Exposure to sunlight adds to its strength. Sunlight also makes the bud on its back grow larger.

3.sword: Its plant blooms when it is absorbing solar energy. It stays on the move to seek sunlight.
3.shield: A bewitching aroma wafts from its flower. The fragrance becalms those engaged in a battle.

4.sword: It has a preference for hot things. When it rains, steam is said to spout from the tip of its tail.
4.shield: From the time it is born, a flame burns at the tip of its tail. Its life would end if the flame were to go out.

5.sword: It has a barbaric nature. In battle, it whips its fiery tail around and slashes away with sharp claws.
5.shield: If it becomes agitated during battle, it spouts intense flames, incinerating its surroundings.

6.sword: It spits fire that is hot enough to melt boulders. It may cause forest fires by blowing flames.
6.shield: Its wings can carry this Pokémon close to an altitude of 4,600 feet. It blows out fire at very high temperatures.

7.sword: When it retracts its long neck into its shell, it squirts out water with vigorous force.
7.shield: When it feels threatened, it draws its limbs inside its shell and sprays water from its mouth.

8.sword: It is recognized as a symbol of longevity. If its shell has algae on it, that Wartortle is very old.
8.shield: It cleverly controls its furry ears and tail to maintain its balance while swimming.

9.sword: It crushes its foe under its heavy body to cause fainting. In a pinch, it will withdraw inside its shell.
9.shield: The rocket cannons on its shell fire jets of water capable of punching holes through thick steel.

10.sword: For protection, it releases a horrible stench from the antenna on its head to drive away enemies.
10.shield: Its short feet are tipped with suction pads that enable it to tirelessly climb slopes and walls.

11.sword: It is waiting for the moment to evolve. At this stage, it can only harden, so it remains motionless to avoid attack.
11.shield: Even though it is encased in a sturdy shell, the body inside is tender. It can’t withstand a harsh attack.

12.sword: In battle, it flaps its wings at great speed to release highly toxic dust into the air.
12.shield: It collects honey every day. It rubs honey onto the hairs on its legs to carry it back to its nest.

25.sword: Pikachu that can generate powerful electricity have cheek sacs that are extra soft and super stretchy.
25.shield: When Pikachu meet, they’ll touch their tails together and exchange electricity through them as a form of greeting.

26.sword: Its long tail serves as a ground to protect itself from its own high-voltage power.
26.shield: If its electric pouches run empty, it raises its tail to gather electricity from the atmosphere.

27.sword: It loves to bathe in the grit of dry, sandy areas. By sand bathing, the Pokémon rids itself of dirt and moisture clinging to its body.
27.shield: It burrows into the ground to create its nest. If hard stones impede its tunneling, it uses its sharp claws to shatter them and then carries on digging.

28.sword: The drier the area Sandslash lives in, the harder and smoother the Pokémon’s spikes will feel when touched.
28.shield: It climbs trees by hooking on with its sharp claws. Sandslash shares the berries it gathers, dropping them down to Sandshrew waiting below the tree.

29.sword: Females are more sensitive to smells than males. While foraging, they’ll use their whiskers to check wind direction and stay downwind of predators.
29.shield: It uses its hard incisor teeth to crush and eat berries. The tip of a female Nidoran’s horn is a bit more rounded than the tip of a male’s horn.

30.sword: The horn on its head has atrophied. It’s thought that this happens so Nidorina’s children won’t get poked while their mother is feeding them.
30.shield: If the group is threatened, these Pokémon will band together to assault enemies with a chorus of ultrasonic waves.

31.sword: Nidoqueen is better at defense than offense. With scales like armor, this Pokémon will shield its children from any kind of attack.
31.shield: It pacifies offspring by placing them in the gaps between the spines on its back. The spines will never secrete poison while young are present.

32.sword: The horn on a male Nidoran’s forehead contains a powerful poison. This is a very cautious Pokémon, always straining its large ears.
32.shield: Small but brave, this Pokémon will hold its ground and even risk its life in battle to protect the female it’s friendly with.

33.sword: With a horn that’s harder than diamond, this Pokémon goes around shattering boulders as it searches for a moon stone.
33.shield: It’s nervous and quick to act aggressively. The potency of its poison increases along with the level of adrenaline present in its body.

34.sword: When it goes on a rampage, it’s impossible to control. But in the presence of a Nidoqueen it’s lived with for a long time, Nidoking calms down.
34.shield: Nidoking prides itself on its strength. It’s forceful and spirited in battle, making use of its thick tail and diamond-crushing horn.

35.sword: It is said that happiness will come to those who see a gathering of Clefairy dancing under a full moon.
35.shield: Its adorable behavior and cry make it highly popular. However, this cute Pokémon is rarely found.

36.sword: A timid fairy Pokémon that is rarely seen, it will run and hide the moment it senses people.
36.shield: Their ears are sensitive enough to hear a pin drop from over a mile away, so they’re usually found in quiet places.

37.sword: While young, it has six gorgeous tails. When it grows, several new tails are sprouted.
37.shield: As each tail grows, its fur becomes more lustrous. When held, it feels slightly warm.

38.sword: It is said to live 1,000 years, and each of its tails is loaded with supernatural powers.
38.shield: Very smart and very vengeful. Grabbing one of its many tails could result in a 1,000-year curse.

39.sword: Jigglypuff has top-notch lung capacity, even by comparison to other Pokémon. It won’t stop singing its lullabies until its foes fall asleep.
39.shield: By freely changing the wavelength of its voice, Jigglypuff sings a mysterious melody sure to make any listener sleepy.

40.sword: The more air it takes in, the more it inflates. If opponents catch it in a bad mood, it will inflate itself to an enormous size to intimidate them.
40.shield: It’s proud of its fur, which is fine and delicate. In particular, the curl on its forehead has a texture that’s perfectly heavenly.

41.sword: It emits ultrasonic waves from its mouth to check its surroundings. Even in tight caves, Zubat flies around with skill.
41.shield: Zubat live in caves, down where the sun’s light won’t reach. In the morning, they gather together to keep each other warm as they sleep.

42.sword: It loves to drink other creatures’ blood. It’s said that if it finds others of its kind going hungry, it sometimes shares the blood it’s gathered.
42.shield: Its feet are tiny, but this Pokémon walks skillfully. It sneaks up on sleeping prey before sinking in its fangs and slurping up blood.

43.sword: If exposed to moonlight, it starts to move. It roams far and wide at night to scatter its seeds.
43.shield: During the day, it stays in the cold underground to avoid the sun. It grows by bathing in moonlight.

44.sword: Its pistils exude an incredibly foul odor. The horrid stench can cause fainting at a distance of 1.25 miles.
44.shield: What appears to be drool is actually sweet honey. It is very sticky and clings stubbornly if touched.

45.sword: It has the world’s largest petals. With every step, the petals shake out heavy clouds of toxic pollen.
45.shield: The larger its petals, the more toxic pollen it contains. Its big head is heavy and hard to hold up.

50.sword: If a Diglett digs through a field, it leaves the soil perfectly tilled and ideal for planting crops.
50.shield: It burrows through the ground at a shallow depth. It leaves raised earth in its wake, making it easy to spot.

51.sword: A team of Diglett triplets. It triggers huge earthquakes by burrowing 60 miles underground.
51.shield: These Diglett triplets dig over 60 miles below sea level. No one knows what it’s like underground.

52.sword: It loves to collect shiny things. If it’s in a good mood, it might even let its Trainer have a look at its hoard of treasures.
52.shield: It washes its face regularly to keep the coin on its forehead spotless. It doesn’t get along with Galarian Meowth.

53.sword: Getting this prideful Pokémon to warm up to you takes a lot of effort, and it will claw at you the moment it gets annoyed.
53.shield: Its elegant and refined behavior clashes with that of the barbaric Perrserker. The relationship between the two is one of mutual disdain.

54.sword: Psyduck is constantly beset by headaches. If the Pokémon lets its strange power erupt, apparently the pain subsides for a while.
54.shield: As Psyduck gets stressed out, its headache gets progressively worse. It uses intense psychic energy to overwhelm those around it.

55.sword: This Pokémon lives in gently flowing rivers. It paddles through the water with its long limbs, putting its graceful swimming skills on display.
55.shield: Old tales tell of Golduck punishing those that defiled its river. The guilty were dragged into the water and taken away.

58.sword: It has a brave and trustworthy nature. It fearlessly stands up to bigger and stronger foes.
58.shield: Extremely loyal, it will fearlessly bark at any opponent to protect its own Trainer from harm.

59.sword: The sight of it running over 6,200 miles in a single day and night has captivated many people.
59.shield: A Pokémon that has long been admired for its beauty. It runs agilely as if on wings.

60.sword: For Poliwag, swimming is easier than walking. The swirl pattern on its belly is actually part of the Pokémon’s innards showing through the skin.
60.shield: In rivers with fast-flowing water, this Pokémon will cling to a rock by using its thick lips, which act like a suction cup.

61.sword: Staring at the swirl on its belly causes drowsiness. This trait of Poliwhirl’s has been used in place of lullabies to get children to go to sleep.
61.shield: This Pokémon’s sweat is a slimy mucus. When captured, Poliwhirl can slither from its enemies’ grasp and escape.

62.sword: Its body is solid muscle. When swimming through cold seas, Poliwrath uses its impressive arms to smash through drift ice and plow forward.
62.shield: Poliwrath is skilled at both swimming and martial arts. It uses its well-trained arms to dish out powerful punches.

63.sword: This Pokémon uses its psychic powers while it sleeps. The contents of Abra’s dreams affect the powers that the Pokémon wields.
63.shield: Abra can teleport in its sleep. Apparently the more deeply Abra sleeps, the farther its teleportations go.

64.sword: Using its psychic power, Kadabra levitates as it sleeps. It uses its springy tail as a pillow.
64.shield: This Pokémon’s telekinesis is immensely powerful. To prepare for evolution, Kadabra stores up psychic energy in the star on its forehead.

65.sword: It has an incredibly high level of intelligence. Some say that Alakazam remembers everything that ever happens to it, from birth till death.
65.shield: Alakazam wields potent psychic powers. It’s said that this Pokémon used these powers to create the spoons it holds.

66.sword: Its whole body is composed of muscles. Even though it’s the size of a human child, it can hurl 100 grown-ups.
66.shield: Always brimming with power, it passes time by lifting boulders. Doing so makes it even stronger.

67.sword: Its muscular body is so powerful, it must wear a power-save belt to be able to regulate its motions.
67.shield: Its formidable body never gets tired. It helps people by doing work such as the moving of heavy goods.

68.sword: It quickly swings its four arms to rock its opponents with ceaseless punches and chops from all angles.
68.shield: With four arms that react more quickly than it can think, it can execute many punches at once.

72.sword: Tentacool is not a particularly strong swimmer. It drifts across the surface of shallow seas as it searches for prey.
72.shield: This Pokémon is mostly made of water. A Tentacool out in the ocean is very hard to spot, because its body blends in with the sea.

73.sword: When the red orbs on Tentacruel’s head glow brightly, watch out. The Pokémon is about to fire off a burst of ultrasonic waves.
73.shield: Its 80 tentacles can stretch and shrink freely. Tentacruel ensnares prey in a net of spread-out tentacles, delivering venomous stings to its catch.

77.sword: It can’t run properly when it’s newly born. As it races around with others of its kind, its legs grow stronger.
77.shield: If you’ve been accepted by Ponyta, its burning mane is mysteriously no longer hot to the touch.

78.sword: This Pokémon can be seen galloping through fields at speeds of up to 150 mph, its fiery mane fluttering in the wind.
78.shield: The fastest runner becomes the leader, and it decides the herd’s pace and direction of travel.

79.sword: Slow-witted and oblivious, this Pokémon won’t feel any pain if its tail gets eaten. It won’t notice when its tail grows back, either.
79.shield: When this Pokémon’s tail is soaked in water, sweetness seeps from it. Slowpoke uses this trait to lure in and fish up other Pokémon.

80.sword: Slowpoke became Slowbro when a Shellder bit on to its tail. Sweet flavors seeping from the tail make the Shellder feel as if its life is a dream.
80.shield: Being bitten by a Shellder shocked this Pokémon into standing on two legs. If the Shellder lets go, it seems Slowbro will turn back into a Slowpoke.

81.sword: At times, Magnemite runs out of electricity and ends up on the ground. If you give batteries to a grounded Magnemite, it’ll start moving again.
81.shield: It subsists on electricity. As Magnemite flies, it emits electromagnetic waves from the units on each side of its body.

82.sword: This Pokémon is three Magnemite that have linked together. Magneton sends out powerful radio waves to study its surroundings.
82.shield: This Pokémon is constantly putting out a powerful magnetic force. Most computers go haywire when a Magneton approaches.

83.sword: The stalk this Pokémon carries in its wings serves as a sword to cut down opponents. In a dire situation, the stalk can also serve as food.
83.shield: They use a plant stalk as a weapon, but not all of them use it in the same way. Several distinct styles of stalk fighting have been observed.

90.sword: It swims facing backward by opening and closing its two-piece shell. It is surprisingly fast.
90.shield: Its hard shell repels any kind of attack. It is vulnerable only when its shell is open.

91.sword: Its shell is extremely hard. It cannot be shattered, even with a bomb. The shell opens only when it is attacking.
91.shield: Once it slams its shell shut, it is impossible to open, even by those with superior strength.

92.sword: Born from gases, anyone would faint if engulfed by its gaseous body, which contains poison.
92.shield: With its gas-like body, it can sneak into any place it desires. However, it can be blown away by wind.

93.sword: Its tongue is made of gas. If licked, its victim starts shaking constantly until death eventually comes.
93.shield: If you get the feeling of being watched in darkness when nobody is around, Haunter is there.

94.sword: On the night of a full moon, if shadows move on their own and laugh, it must be Gengar’s doing.
94.shield: It is said to emerge from darkness to steal the lives of those who become lost in mountains.

95.sword: As it digs through the ground, it absorbs many hard objects. This is what makes its body so solid.
95.shield: It rapidly bores through the ground at 50 mph by squirming and twisting its massive, rugged body.

98.sword: It can be found near the sea. The large pincers grow back if they are torn out of their sockets.
98.shield: If it senses danger approaching, it cloaks itself with bubbles from its mouth so it will look bigger.

99.sword: Its large and hard pincer has 10,000-horsepower strength. However, being so big, it is unwieldy to move.
99.shield: Its oversized claw is very powerful, but when it’s not in battle, the claw just gets in the way.

102.sword: Though it may look like it’s just a bunch of eggs, it’s a proper Pokémon. Exeggcute communicates with others of its kind via telepathy, apparently.
102.shield: These Pokémon get nervous when they’re not in a group of six. The minute even one member of the group goes missing, Exeggcute become cowardly.

103.sword: Each of Exeggutor’s three heads is thinking different thoughts. The three don’t seem to be very interested in one another.
103.shield: When they work together, Exeggutor’s three heads can put out powerful psychic energy. Cloudy days make this Pokémon sluggish.

104.sword: When the memory of its departed mother brings it to tears, its cries echo mournfully within the skull it wears on its head.
104.shield: This Pokémon wears the skull of its deceased mother. Sometimes Cubone’s dreams make it cry, but each tear Cubone sheds makes it stronger.

105.sword: This Pokémon overcame its sorrow to evolve a sturdy new body. Marowak faces its opponents bravely, using a bone as a weapon.
105.shield: When this Pokémon evolved, the skull of its mother fused to it. Marowak’s temperament also turned vicious at the same time.

106.sword: This amazing Pokémon has an awesome sense of balance. It can kick in succession from any position.
106.shield: The legs freely contract and stretch. The stretchy legs allow it to hit a distant foe with a rising kick.

107.sword: Its punches slice the air. They are launched at such high speed, even a slight graze could cause a burn.
107.shield: Its punches slice the air. However, it seems to need a short break after fighting for three minutes.

108.sword: If this Pokémon’s sticky saliva gets on you and you don’t clean it off, an intense itch will set in. The itch won’t go away, either.
108.shield: Bug Pokémon are Lickitung’s main food source. This Pokémon paralyzes its prey with a lick from its long tongue, then swallows the prey whole.

109.sword: Its body is full of poisonous gas. It floats into garbage dumps, seeking out the fumes of raw, rotting trash.
109.shield: It adores polluted air. Some claim that Koffing used to be more plentiful in the Galar region than they are now.

110.sword: It mixes gases between its two bodies. It’s said that these Pokémon were seen all over the Galar region back in the day.
110.shield: It can’t suck in air quite as well as a Galarian Weezing, but the toxins it creates are more potent than those of its counterpart.

111.sword: Strong, but not too bright, this Pokémon can shatter even a skyscraper with its charging tackles.
111.shield: It can remember only one thing at a time. Once it starts rushing, it forgets why it started.

112.sword: It begins walking on its hind legs after evolution. It can punch holes through boulders with its horn.
112.shield: Protected by an armor-like hide, it is capable of living in molten lava of 3,600 degrees Fahrenheit.

113.sword: The egg Chansey carries is not only delicious but also packed with nutrition. It’s used as a high-class cooking ingredient.
113.shield: This species was once very slow. To protect their eggs from other creatures, these Pokémon became able to flee quickly.

114.sword: Hidden beneath a tangle of vines that grows nonstop even if the vines are torn off, this Pokémon’s true appearance remains a mystery.
114.shield: The vines of a Tangela have a distinct scent. In some parts of Galar, Tangela vines are used as herbs.

115.sword: Although it’s carrying its baby in a pouch on its belly, Kangaskhan is swift on its feet. It intimidates its opponents with quick jabs.
115.shield: There are records of a lost human child being raised by a childless Kangaskhan.

116.sword: Horsea makes its home in oceans with gentle currents. If this Pokémon is under attack, it spits out pitch-black ink and escapes.
116.shield: They swim with dance-like motions and cause whirlpools to form. Horsea compete to see which of them can generate the biggest whirlpool.

117.sword: It’s the males that raise the offspring. While Seadra are raising young, the spines on their backs secrete thicker and stronger poison.
117.shield: Seadra’s mouth is slender, but its suction power is strong. In an instant, Seadra can suck in food that’s larger than the opening of its mouth.

118.sword: Its dorsal, pectoral, and tail fins wave elegantly in water. That is why it is known as the Water Dancer.
118.shield: Its dorsal and pectoral fins are strongly developed like muscles. It can swim at a speed of five knots.

119.sword: In autumn, its body becomes more fatty in preparing to propose to a mate. It takes on beautiful colors.
119.shield: Using its horn, it bores holes in riverbed boulders, making nests to prevent its eggs from washing away.

120.sword: If you visit a beach at the end of summer, you’ll be able to see groups of Staryu lighting up in a steady rhythm.
120.shield: Fish Pokémon nibble at it, but Staryu isn’t bothered. Its body regenerates quickly, even if part of it is completely torn off.

121.sword: This Pokémon has an organ known as its core. The organ glows in seven colors when Starmie is unleashing its potent psychic powers.
121.shield: Starmie swims by spinning its body at high speed. As this Pokémon cruises through the ocean, it absorbs tiny plankton.

122.sword: The broadness of its hands may be no coincidence—many scientists believe its palms became enlarged specifically for pantomiming.
122.shield: It’s known for its top-notch pantomime skills. It protects itself from all sorts of attacks by emitting auras from its fingers to create walls.

123.sword: As Scyther fights more and more battles, its scythes become sharper and sharper. With a single slice, Scyther can fell a massive tree.
123.shield: If you come across an area in a forest where a lot of the trees have been cut down, what you’ve found is a Scyther’s territory.

124.sword: In certain parts of Galar, Jynx was once feared and worshiped as the Queen of Ice.
124.shield: The Jynx of Galar often have beautiful and delicate voices. Some of these Pokémon have even gathered a fan base.

125.sword: Many power plants keep Ground-type Pokémon around as a defense against Electabuzz that come seeking electricity.
125.shield: With the coming of a storm, many of these Pokémon will gather under tall trees and sit there waiting for lightning to strike.

126.sword: Magmar dispatches its prey with fire. But it regrets this habit once it realizes that it has burned its intended prey to a charred crisp.
126.shield: These Pokémon’s bodies are constantly burning. Magmar are feared as one of the causes behind fires.

127.sword: These Pokémon judge one another based on pincers. Thicker, more impressive pincers make for more popularity with the opposite gender.
127.shield: This Pokémon clamps its pincers down on its prey and then either splits the prey in half or flings it away.

128.sword: When Tauros begins whipping itself with its tails, it’s a warning that the Pokémon is about to charge with astounding speed.
128.shield: The Tauros of the Galar region are volatile in nature, and they won’t allow people to ride on their backs.

129.sword: It is virtually worthless in terms of both power and speed. It is the most weak and pathetic Pokémon in the world.
129.shield: This weak and pathetic Pokémon gets easily pushed along rivers when there are strong currents.

130.sword: It has an extremely aggressive nature. The Hyper Beam it shoots from its mouth totally incinerates all targets.
130.shield: Once it begins to rampage, a Gyarados will burn everything down, even in a harsh storm.

131.sword: A smart and kindhearted Pokémon, it glides across the surface of the sea while its beautiful song echoes around it.
131.shield: Crossing icy seas is no issue for this cold-resistant Pokémon. Its smooth skin is a little cool to the touch.

132.sword: It can reconstitute its entire cellular structure to change into what it sees, but it returns to normal when it relaxes.
132.shield: When it encounters another Ditto, it will move faster than normal to duplicate that opponent exactly.

133.sword: It has the ability to alter the composition of its body to suit its surrounding environment.
133.shield: Thanks to its unstable genetic makeup, this special Pokémon conceals many different possible evolutions.

134.sword: When Vaporeon’s fins begin to vibrate, it is a sign that rain will come within a few hours.
134.shield: Its body’s cellular structure is similar to the molecular composition of water. It can melt invisibly in water.

135.sword: If it is angered or startled, the fur all over its body bristles like sharp needles that pierce foes.
135.shield: It accumulates negative ions in the atmosphere to blast out 10,000-volt lightning bolts.

136.sword: Once it has stored up enough heat, this Pokémon’s body temperature can reach up to 1,700 degrees Fahrenheit.
136.shield: It stores some of the air it inhales in its internal flame pouch, which heats it to over 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit.

137.sword: State-of-the-art technology was used to create Porygon. It was the first artificial Pokémon to be created via computer programming.
137.shield: In recent years, this species has been very helpful in cyberspace. These Pokémon will go around checking to make sure no suspicious data exists.

138.sword: Because some Omanyte manage to escape after being restored or are released into the wild by people, this species is becoming a problem.
138.shield: This Pokémon is a member of an ancient, extinct species. Omanyte paddles through water with its 10 tentacles, looking like it’s just drifting along.

139.sword: Weighed down by a large and heavy shell, Omastar couldn’t move very fast. Some say it went extinct because it was unable to catch food.
139.shield: Omastar’s sharp fangs could crush rock, but the Pokémon can attack only the prey that come within reach of its tentacles.

140.sword: This species is almost entirely extinct. Kabuto molt every three days, making their shells harder and harder.
140.shield: While some say this species has gone extinct, Kabuto sightings are apparently fairly common in some places.

141.sword: Kabutops slices its prey apart and sucks out the fluids. The discarded body parts become food for other Pokémon.
141.shield: The cause behind the extinction of this species is unknown. Kabutops were aggressive Pokémon that inhabited warm seas.

142.sword: This is a ferocious Pokémon from ancient times. Apparently even modern technology is incapable of producing a perfectly restored specimen.
142.shield: Aerodactyl’s sawlike fangs can shred skin to tatters—even the skin of Steel-type Pokémon.

143.sword: It is not satisfied unless it eats over 880 pounds of food every day. When it is done eating, it goes promptly to sleep.
143.shield: This Pokémon’s stomach is so strong, even eating moldy or rotten food will not affect it.

144.sword: It’s said that this Pokémon’s beautiful blue wings are made of ice. Articuno flies over snowy mountains, its long tail fluttering along behind it.
144.shield: This Pokémon can control ice at will. Articuno is said to live in snowy mountains riddled with permafrost.

145.sword: This Pokémon has complete control over electricity. There are tales of Zapdos nesting in the dark depths of pitch-black thunderclouds.
145.shield: Zapdos is a legendary bird Pokémon. It’s said that when Zapdos rubs its feathers together, lightning will fall immediately after.

146.sword: It’s one of the legendary bird Pokémon. When Moltres flaps its flaming wings, they glimmer with a dazzling red glow.
146.shield: There are stories of this Pokémon using its radiant, flame-cloaked wings to light up paths for those lost in the mountains.

147.sword: Dratini dwells near bodies of rapidly flowing water, such as the plunge pools of waterfalls. As it grows, Dratini will shed its skin many times.
147.shield: This Pokémon was long considered to be no more than a myth. The small lump on a Dratini’s forehead is actually a horn that’s still coming in.

148.sword: This Pokémon lives in pristine oceans and lakes. It can control the weather, and it uses this power to fly into the sky, riding on the wind.
148.shield: This Pokémon gathers power in the orbs on its tail and controls the weather. When enshrouded by an aura, Dragonair has a mystical appearance.

149.sword: It’s a kindhearted Pokémon. If it spots a drowning person or Pokémon, Dragonite simply must help them.
149.shield: This Pokémon is known as the Sea Incarnate. Figureheads that resemble Dragonite decorate the bows of many ships.

163.sword: It always stands on one foot. It changes feet so fast, the movement can rarely be seen.
163.shield: It begins to hoot at the same time every day. Some Trainers use them in place of clocks.

164.sword: Its eyes are specially developed to enable it to see clearly even in murky darkness and minimal light.
164.shield: When it needs to think, it rotates its head 180 degrees to sharpen its intellectual power.

169.sword: Both of its legs have turned into wings. Without a sound, Crobat flies swiftly toward its prey and sinks its fangs into the nape of its target’s neck.
169.shield: This Pokémon flaps its four wings skillfully. Crobat can fly through cramped caves without needing to slow down.

170.sword: Its antennae, which evolved from a fin, have both positive and negative charges flowing through them.
170.shield: On the dark ocean floor, its only means of communication is its constantly flashing lights.

171.sword: The light it emits is so bright that it can illuminate the sea’s surface from a depth of over three miles.
171.shield: This Pokémon flashes a bright light that blinds its prey. This creates an opening for it to deliver an electrical attack.

172.sword: Despite its small size, it can zap even adult humans. However, if it does so, it also surprises itself.
172.shield: The electric sacs in its cheeks are small. If even a little electricity leaks, it becomes shocked.

173.sword: According to local rumors, Cleffa are often seen in places where shooting stars have fallen.
173.shield: Because of its unusual, starlike silhouette, people believe that it came here on a meteor.

174.sword: Igglybuff loves to sing. Its marshmallow-like body gives off a faint sweet smell.
174.shield: Taking advantage of the softness of its body, Igglybuff moves as if bouncing. Its body turns a deep pink when its temperature rises.

175.sword: The shell seems to be filled with joy. It is said that it will share good luck when treated kindly.
175.shield: It is considered to be a symbol of good luck. Its shell is said to be filled with happiness.

176.sword: They say that it will appear before kindhearted, caring people and shower them with happiness.
176.shield: It grows dispirited if it is not with kind people. It can float in midair without moving its wings.

177.sword: It is extremely good at climbing tree trunks and likes to eat the new sprouts on the trees.
177.shield: Because its wings aren’t yet fully grown, it has to hop to get around. It is always staring at something.

178.sword: They say that it stays still and quiet because it is seeing both the past and future at the same time.
178.shield: This odd Pokémon can see both the past and the future. It eyes the sun’s movement all day.

182.sword: Plentiful in the tropics. When it dances, its petals rub together and make a pleasant ringing sound.
182.shield: Bellossom gather at times and appear to dance. They say that the dance is a ritual to summon the sun.

183.sword: This Pokémon uses its round tail as a float. The ball of Marill’s tail is filled with nutrients that have been turned into an oil.
183.shield: Even after Marill swims in a cold sea, its water- repellent fur dries almost as soon as Marill leaves the water. That’s why this Pokémon is never cold.

184.sword: It spends most of its time in the water. On sunny days, Azumarill floats on the surface of the water and sunbathes.
184.shield: These Pokémon create air-filled bubbles. When Azurill play in rivers, Azumarill will cover them with these bubbles.

185.sword: If a tree branch shakes when there is no wind, it’s a Sudowoodo, not a tree. It hides from the rain.
185.shield: It disguises itself as a tree to avoid attack. It hates water, so it will disappear if it starts raining.

186.sword: At nightfall, these Pokémon appear on the shores of lakes. They announce their territorial claims by letting out cries that sound like shouting.
186.shield: The cry of a male is louder than that of a female. Male Politoed with deep, menacing voices find more popularity with the opposite gender.

194.sword: This Pokémon lives in cold water. It will leave the water to search for food when it gets cold outside.
194.shield: When walking on land, it covers its body with a poisonous film that keeps its skin from dehydrating.

195.sword: It has an easygoing nature. It doesn’t care if it bumps its head on boats and boulders while swimming.
195.shield: Its body is always slimy. It often bangs its head on the river bottom as it swims but seems not to care.

196.sword: By reading air currents, it can predict things such as the weather or its foe’s next move.
196.shield: It unleashes psychic power from the orb on its forehead. When its power is exhausted, the orb grows dull and dark.

197.sword: When this Pokémon becomes angry, its pores secrete a poisonous sweat, which it sprays at its opponent’s eyes.
197.shield: On the night of a full moon, or when it gets excited, the ring patterns on its body glow yellow.

199.sword: Miraculously, this former Slowpoke’s latent intelligence was drawn out when Shellder poison raced through its brain.
199.shield: Slowking can solve any problem presented to it, but no one can understand a thing Slowking says.

202.sword: It hates light and shock. If attacked, it inflates its body to pump up its counterstrike.
202.shield: To keep its pitch-black tail hidden, it lives quietly in the darkness. It is never first to attack.

206.sword: This Pokémon’s tiny wings have some scientists saying that Dunsparce used to fly through the sky in ancient times.
206.shield: The nests Dunsparce live in are mazes of tunnels. They never get lost in their own nests—they can tell where they are by the scent of the dirt.

208.sword: It is said that if an Onix lives for over 100 years, its composition changes to become diamond-like.
208.shield: It is thought its body transformed as a result of iron accumulating internally from swallowing soil.

211.sword: When faced with a larger opponent, it swallows as much water as it can to match the opponent’s size.
211.shield: The small spikes covering its body developed from scales. They inject a toxin that causes fainting.

212.sword: Bulky pincers account for one third of Scizor’s body weight. A single swing of one of these pincers will crush a boulder completely.
212.shield: Though its body is slim, Scizor has tremendous attacking power. Even Scizor’s muscles are made of metal.

213.sword: It stores berries inside its shell. To avoid attacks, it hides beneath rocks and remains completely still.
213.shield: The berries stored in its vaselike shell eventually become a thick, pulpy juice.

214.sword: Heracross loves sweet sap and will go looking through forests for it. The Pokémon uses its two antennae to pick up scents as it searches.
214.shield: This Pokémon takes pride in its strength, which allows it to lift things 100 times heavier than itself with no trouble at all.

215.sword: Its paws conceal sharp claws. If attacked, it suddenly extends the claws and startles its enemy.
215.shield: It has a cunning yet savage disposition. It waits for parents to leave their nests, and then it sneaks in to steal their eggs.

220.sword: It rubs its snout on the ground to find and dig up food. It sometimes discovers hot springs.
220.shield: If it smells something enticing, it dashes off headlong to find the source of the aroma.

221.sword: If it charges at an enemy, the hairs on its back stand up straight. It is very sensitive to sound.
221.shield: Although its legs are short, its rugged hooves prevent it from slipping, even on icy ground.

222.sword: It will regrow any branches that break off its head. People keep particularly beautiful Corsola branches as charms to promote safe childbirth.
222.shield: These Pokémon live in warm seas. In prehistoric times, many lived in the oceans around the Galar region as well.

223.sword: The water they shoot from their mouths can hit moving prey from more than 300 feet away.
223.shield: Using its dorsal fin as a suction pad, it clings to a Mantine’s underside to scavenge for leftovers.

224.sword: It has a tendency to want to be in holes. It prefers rock crags or pots and sprays ink from them before attacking.
224.shield: It traps enemies with its suction-cupped tentacles, then smashes them with its rock-hard head.

225.sword: It carries food all day long. There are tales about lost people who were saved by the food it had.
225.shield: It has a generous habit of sharing its food with people and Pokémon, so it’s always scrounging around for more food.

226.sword: If it builds up enough speed swimming, it can jump out above the waves and glide for over 300 feet.
226.shield: As it majestically swims, it doesn’t care if Remoraid attach to it to scavenge for its leftovers.

227.sword: The pointed feathers of these Pokémon are sharper than swords. Skarmory and Corviknight fight viciously over territory.
227.shield: People fashion swords from Skarmory’s shed feathers, so this Pokémon is a popular element in heraldic designs.

230.sword: With the arrival of a storm at sea, this Pokémon will show itself on the surface. When a Kingdra and a Dragonite meet, a fierce battle ensues.
230.shield: Scales shed by this Pokémon have such a splendorous gleam to them that they’ve been given to royalty as gifts.

233.sword: This is a Porygon that was updated with special data. Porygon2 develops itself by learning about many different subjects all on its own.
233.shield: After artificial intelligence was implemented in Porygon2, the Pokémon began using a strange language that only other Porygon2 understand.

236.sword: It is always bursting with energy. To make itself stronger, it keeps on fighting even if it loses.
236.shield: Even though it is small, it can’t be ignored because it will slug any handy target without warning.

237.sword: It launches kicks while spinning. If it spins at high speed, it may bore its way into the ground.
237.shield: After doing a handstand to throw off the opponent’s timing, it presents its fancy kick moves.

238.sword: If its face gets even slightly dirty, Smoochum will bathe immediately. But if its body gets dirty, Smoochum doesn’t really seem to care.
238.shield: This is a very curious Pokémon. Smoochum decides what it likes and dislikes by touching things with its lips.

239.sword: When a storm approaches, this Pokémon gets restless. Once Elekid hears the sound of thunder, it gets full-on rowdy.
239.shield: It’s not good at storing electricity yet. This Pokémon sneaks into people’s homes, looking for electrical outlets to eat electricity from.

240.sword: This Pokémon is still small and timid. Whenever Magby gets excited or surprised, flames leak from its mouth and its nose.
240.shield: This Pokémon makes its home near volcanoes. At the end of the day, Magby soaks in magma, resting and recovering from the day’s fatigue.

241.sword: Miltank produces highly nutritious milk, so it’s been supporting the lives of people and other Pokémon since ancient times.
241.shield: This Pokémon needs to be milked every day, or else it will fall ill. The flavor of Miltank milk changes with the seasons.

242.sword: Whenever a Blissey finds a weakened Pokémon, it will share its egg and offer its care until the other Pokémon is all better.
242.shield: Blissey lays mysterious eggs that are filled with happiness. It’s said that anyone who eats a Blissey egg will start acting kindly to all others.

246.sword: Born deep underground, it comes aboveground and becomes a pupa once it has finished eating the surrounding soil.
246.shield: It feeds on soil. After it has eaten a large mountain, it will fall asleep so it can grow.

247.sword: Even sealed in its shell, it can move freely. Hard and fast, it has outstanding destructive power.
247.shield: It will not stay still, even while it’s a pupa. It already has arms and legs under its solid shell.

248.sword: Its body can’t be harmed by any sort of attack, so it is very eager to make challenges against enemies.
248.shield: The quakes caused when it walks make even great mountains crumble and change the surrounding terrain.

251.sword: This Pokémon has the ability to move through time. Records describing it as a forest deity can be found from many different eras.
251.shield: This Pokémon traveled through time to come from the future. It bolsters grass and trees with its own strength, and it can heal wounds, too.

263.sword: It marks its territory by rubbing its bristly fur on trees. This variety of Zigzagoon is friendlier and calmer than the kind native to Galar.
263.shield: Zigzagoon that adapted to regions outside Galar acquired this appearance. If you’ve lost something, this Pokémon can likely find it.

264.sword: Its fur is strong and supple. Shaving brushes made with shed Linoone hairs are highly prized.
264.shield: It uses its explosive speed and razor-sharp claws to bring down prey. Running along winding paths is not its strong suit.

270.sword: It searches about for clean water. If it does not drink water for too long, the leaf on its head wilts.
270.shield: Its leaf grew too large for it to live on land. That is how it began to live floating in the water.

271.sword: It is nocturnal and becomes active at nightfall. It feeds on aquatic mosses that grow in the riverbed.
271.shield: It lives at the water’s edge where it is sunny. It sleeps on a bed of water grass by day and becomes active at night.

272.sword: The rhythm of bright, festive music activates Ludicolo’s cells, making it more powerful.
272.shield: If it hears festive music, it begins moving in rhythm in order to amplify its power.

273.sword: If it remains still, it looks just like a real nut. It delights in surprising foraging Pokémon.
273.shield: It attaches itself to a tree branch using the top of its head. Strong winds can sometimes make it fall.

274.sword: It lives deep in forests. With the leaf on its head, it makes a flute whose song makes listeners uneasy.
274.shield: They live in holes bored in large trees. The sound of Nuzleaf’s grass flute fills listeners with dread.

275.sword: A Pokémon that was feared as a forest guardian. It can read the foe’s mind and take preemptive action.
275.shield: It lives quietly in the deep forest. It is said to create chilly winter winds with the fans it holds.

278.sword: It makes its nest on sheer cliffs. Riding the sea breeze, it glides up into the expansive skies.
278.shield: It soars on updrafts without flapping its wings. It makes a nest on sheer cliffs at the sea’s edge.

279.sword: It is a messenger of the skies, carrying small Pokémon and eggs to safety in its bill.
279.shield: Skimming the water’s surface, it dips its large bill in the sea, scoops up food and water, and carries it.

280.sword: It is highly attuned to the emotions of people and Pokémon. It hides if it senses hostility.
280.shield: If its horns capture the warm feelings of people or Pokémon, its body warms up slightly.

281.sword: If its Trainer becomes happy, it overflows with energy, dancing joyously while spinning about.
281.shield: It has a psychic power that enables it to distort the space around it and see into the future.

282.sword: It has the power to predict the future. Its power peaks when it is protecting its Trainer.
282.shield: To protect its Trainer, it will expend all its psychic power to create a small black hole.

290.sword: Because it lived almost entirely underground, it is nearly blind. It uses its antennae instead.
290.shield: It can sometimes live underground for more than 10 years. It absorbs nutrients from the roots of trees.

291.sword: Its cry leaves a lasting headache if heard for too long. It moves so quickly that it is almost invisible.
291.shield: This Pokémon is so quick, it is said to be able to avoid any attack. It loves to feed on tree sap.

292.sword: A most peculiar Pokémon that somehow appears in a Poké Ball when a Nincada evolves.
292.shield: A strange Pokémon—it flies without moving its wings, has a hollow shell for a body, and does not breathe.

293.sword: The cry of a Whismur is over 100 decibels. If you’re close to a Whismur when it lets out a cry, you’ll be stuck with an all-day headache.
293.shield: When Whismur cries, the sound of its own voice startles it, making the Pokémon cry even louder. It cries until it’s exhausted, then it falls asleep.

294.sword: Loudred’s ears serve as speakers, and they can put out sound waves powerful enough to blow away a house.
294.shield: The force of this Pokémon’s loud voice isn’t just the sound—it’s also the wave of air pressure that blows opponents away and damages them.

295.sword: In the past, people would use the loud voices of these Pokémon as a means of communication between distant cities.
295.shield: This Pokémon can do more than just shout. To communicate with others of its kind, it’ll emit all sorts of sounds from the holes in its body.

298.sword: The ball on Azurill’s tail bounces like a rubber ball, and it’s full of the nutrients the Pokémon needs to grow.
298.shield: Although Azurill are normally docile, an angry one will swing around the big ball on its tail and try to smash its opponents.

302.sword: This Pokémon is feared. When its gemstone eyes begin to glow with a sinister shine, it’s believed that Sableye will steal people’s spirits away.
302.shield: It feeds on gemstone crystals. In darkness, its eyes sparkle with the glitter of jewels.

303.sword: It uses its docile-looking face to lull foes into complacency, then bites with its huge, relentless jaws.
303.shield: It chomps with its gaping mouth. Its huge jaws are actually steel horns that have been transformed.

304.sword: It eats iron ore—and sometimes railroad tracks— to build up the steel armor that protects its body.
304.shield: When Aron evolves, its steel armor peels off. In ancient times, people would collect Aron’s shed armor and make good use of it in their daily lives.

305.sword: Lairon live in mountains brimming with spring water and iron ore, so these Pokémon often came into conflict with humans in the past.
305.shield: During territorial disputes, Lairon fight by slamming into each other. Close inspection of their steel armor reveals scratches and dents.

306.sword: Aggron has a horn sharp enough to perforate thick iron sheets. It brings down its opponents by ramming into them horn first.
306.shield: Long ago, there was a king who wore a helmet meant to resemble the head of an Aggron. He was trying to channel the Pokémon’s strength.

309.sword: It stores static electricity in its fur for discharging. It gives off sparks if a storm approaches.
309.shield: It stores electricity in its fur. It gives off sparks from all over its body in seasons when the air is dry.

310.sword: It stimulates its own muscles with electricity, so it can move quickly. It eases its soreness with electricity, too, so it can recover quickly as well.
310.shield: It rarely appears before people. It is said to nest where lightning has fallen.

315.sword: Its flowers give off a relaxing fragrance. The stronger its aroma, the healthier the Roselia is.
315.shield: It uses the different poisons in each hand separately when it attacks. The stronger its aroma, the healthier it is.

318.sword: It won’t attack while it’s alone—not even if it spots prey. Instead, it waits for other Carvanha to join it, and then the Pokémon attack as a group.
318.shield: These Pokémon have sharp fangs and powerful jaws. Sailors avoid Carvanha dens at all costs.

319.sword: As soon as it catches the scent of prey, Sharpedo will jet seawater from its backside, hurtling toward the target to attack at 75 mph.
319.shield: This Pokémon is known as the Bully of the Sea. Any ship entering the waters Sharpedo calls home will be attacked—no exceptions.

320.sword: It shows off by spraying jets of seawater from the nostrils above its eyes. It eats a solid ton of Wishiwashi every day.
320.shield: When it sucks in a large volume of seawater, it becomes like a big, bouncy ball. It eats a ton of food daily.

321.sword: It can sometimes knock out opponents with the shock created by breaching and crashing its big body onto the water.
321.shield: Its immense size is the reason for its popularity. Wailord watching is a favorite sightseeing activity in various parts of the world.

324.sword: It burns coal inside its shell for energy. It blows out black soot if it is endangered.
324.shield: You find abandoned coal mines full of them. They dig tirelessly in search of coal.

328.sword: Its nest is a sloped, bowl-like pit in the desert. Once something has fallen in, there is no escape.
328.shield: It makes an inescapable conical pit and lies in wait at the bottom for prey to come tumbling down.

329.sword: The ultrasonic waves it generates by rubbing its two wings together cause severe headaches.
329.shield: To help make its wings grow, it dissolves quantities of prey in its digestive juices and guzzles them down every day.

330.sword: This Pokémon hides in the heart of sandstorms it creates and seldom appears where people can see it.
330.shield: It is nicknamed the Desert Spirit because the flapping of its wings sounds like a woman singing.

333.sword: Its cottony wings are full of air, making them light and fluffy to the touch. Swablu takes diligent care of its wings.
333.shield: Since Swablu looks like a cumulus cloud, foes can have a hard time finding it. Apparently its wings turned white over many generations.

334.sword: As it flies in a calm and relaxed manner, Altaria performs a humming song that would enrapture any audience.
334.shield: This Pokémon has a kind disposition, but if it’s provoked, it will threaten opponents with shrill cries before attacking them without mercy.

337.sword: The phase of the moon apparently has some effect on its power. It’s active on the night of a full moon.
337.shield: It was discovered at the site of a meteor strike 40 years ago. Its stare can lull its foes to sleep.

338.sword: When it rotates itself, it gives off light similar to the sun, thus blinding its foes.
338.shield: Solar energy is the source of its power, so it is strong during the daytime. When it spins, its body shines.

339.sword: Its slimy body is hard to grasp. In one region, it is said to have been born from hardened mud.
339.shield: It probes muddy riverbeds with its two long whiskers. A slimy film protects its body.

340.sword: It makes its nest at the bottom of swamps. It will eat anything—if it is alive, Whiscash will eat it.
340.shield: It claims a large swamp to itself. If a foe comes near it, it sets off tremors by thrashing around.

341.sword: No matter how dirty the water in the river, it will adapt and thrive. It has a strong will to survive.
341.shield: It was originally a Pokémon from afar that escaped to the wild. It can adapt to the dirtiest river.

342.sword: A rough customer that wildly flails its giant claws. It is said to be extremely hard to raise.
342.shield: A brutish Pokémon that loves to battle. It will crash itself into any foe that approaches its nest.

343.sword: It moves while spinning around on its single foot. Some Baltoy have been seen spinning on their heads.
343.shield: It was discovered in ancient ruins. While moving, it constantly spins. It stands on one foot even when asleep.

344.sword: This mysterious Pokémon started life as an ancient clay figurine made over 20,000 years ago.
344.shield: It appears to have been born from clay dolls made by ancient people. It uses telekinesis to float and move.

345.sword: This Pokémon was restored from a fossil. Lileep once lived in warm seas that existed approximately 100,000,000 years ago.
345.shield: Lileep clings to rocks on the seabed. When prey comes close, this Pokémon entangles it with petallike tentacles.

346.sword: It has short legs and can’t walk very fast, but its neck and tentacles can extend to over three times their usual length to nab distant prey.
346.shield: Once Cradily catches prey in its tentacles, it digests them whole and absorbs their nutrients.

347.sword: This Pokémon was restored from a fossil. Anorith lived in the ocean about 100,000,000 years ago, hunting with its pair of claws.
347.shield: Anorith can swim swiftly by pulling its eight wings through the water like oars on a boat. This Pokémon is an ancestor of modern bug Pokémon.

348.sword: After evolution, this Pokémon emerged onto land. Its lower body has become stronger, and blows from its tail are devastating.
348.shield: Though it lives on land, it’s also a good swimmer. It dives into the ocean in search of prey, using its sharp claws to take down its quarry.

349.sword: Although unattractive and unpopular, this Pokémon’s marvelous vitality has made it a subject of research.
349.shield: It is a shabby and ugly Pokémon. However, it is very hardy and can survive on little water.

350.sword: Milotic has provided inspiration to many artists. It has even been referred to as the most beautiful Pokémon of all.
350.shield: It’s said that a glimpse of a Milotic and its beauty will calm any hostile emotions you’re feeling.

355.sword: If it finds bad children who won’t listen to their parents, it will spirit them away—or so it’s said.
355.shield: Making itself invisible, it silently sneaks up to prey. It has the ability to slip through thick walls.

356.sword: Its body is entirely hollow. When it opens its mouth, it sucks everything in as if it were a black hole.
356.shield: It seeks drifting will-o’-the-wisps and sucks them into its empty body. What happens inside is a mystery.

359.sword: Swift as the wind, Absol races through fields and mountains. Its curved, bow-like horn is acutely sensitive to the warning signs of natural disasters.
359.shield: Because of this Pokémon’s ability to detect danger, people mistook Absol as a bringer of doom.

360.sword: It tends to move in a pack. Individuals squash against one another to toughen their spirits.
360.shield: It tends to move in a pack with others. They cluster in a tight group to sleep in a cave.

361.sword: It’s said that if they are seen at midnight, they’ll cause heavy snow. They eat snow and ice to survive.
361.shield: It can only survive in cold areas. It bounces happily around, even in environments as cold as −150 degrees Fahrenheit.

362.sword: It has a body of ice that won’t melt, even with fire. It can instantly freeze moisture in the atmosphere.
362.shield: It can instantly freeze moisture in the atmosphere. It uses this power to freeze its foes.

363.sword: This Pokémon’s body is covered in blubber and impressively round. It’s faster for Spheal to roll around than walk.
363.shield: As it drifts among the waves, Spheal probes the sea. As soon as it spots prey, it informs the Walrein in its herd.

364.sword: Sealeo live on top of drift ice. They go swimming when they’re on the hunt, seeking out their prey by scent.
364.shield: This Pokémon has a habit of spinning round things on its nose, whether those things are Poké Balls or Spheal.

365.sword: Walrein form herds of 20 to 30 individuals. When a threat appears, the herd’s leader will protect the group with its life.
365.shield: Walrein’s tusks keep growing throughout its life. Tusks broken in battle will grow back to their usual impressive size in a year.

369.sword: Rock-hard scales and oil-filled swim bladders allow this Pokémon to survive the intense water pressure of the deep sea.
369.shield: This Pokémon was discovered during deep-sea exploration. Its appearance hasn’t changed in 100,000,000 years, so it’s called a living fossil.

371.sword: Bagon jumps off cliffs every day, trying to grow stronger so that someday it will be able to fly.
371.shield: Bagon is a solitary Pokémon that doesn’t form groups with others of its kind. It also has a head hard enough to cleave a boulder in one strike.

372.sword: This Pokémon has covered its body in a hard shell that has the same composition as bone. Shelgon stores energy for evolution.
372.shield: Shelgon ignores its hunger entirely, never eating any food. Apparently, Shelgon will evolve once all its energy stores are used up.

373.sword: Salamence is an unusual Pokémon in that it was able to evolve a body with wings just by constantly wishing to be able to fly.
373.shield: While basking in the joy of flight generally keeps this Pokémon in high spirits, Salamence turns into an uncontrollable menace if something angers it.

374.sword: From its rear, Beldum emits a magnetic force that rapidly pulls opponents in. They get skewered on Beldum’s sharp claws.
374.shield: The cells in this Pokémon’s body are composed of magnetic material. Instead of blood, magnetic forces flow through Beldum’s body.

375.sword: Two Beldum have become stuck together via their own magnetic forces. With two brains, the resulting Metang has doubled psychic powers.
375.shield: Using magnetic forces to stay aloft, this Pokémon flies at high speeds, weaving through harsh mountain terrain in pursuit of prey.

376.sword: Because the magnetic powers of these Pokémon get stronger in freezing temperatures, Metagross living on snowy mountains are full of energy.
376.shield: Metagross is the result of the fusion of two Metang. This Pokémon defeats its opponents through use of its supercomputer-level brain.

377.sword: Every bit of Regirock’s body is made of stone. As parts of its body erode, this Pokémon sticks rocks to itself to repair what’s been lost.
377.shield: Cutting-edge technology was used to study the internals of this Pokémon’s rock body, but nothing was found—not even a brain or a heart.

378.sword: With cold air that can reach temperatures as low as −328 degrees Fahrenheit, Regice instantly freezes any creature that approaches it.
378.shield: This Pokémon’s body is made of solid ice. It’s said that Regice was born beneath thick ice in the ice age.

379.sword: Registeel’s body is made of a strange material that is flexible enough to stretch and shrink but also more durable than any metal.
379.shield: It’s rumored that this Pokémon was born deep underground in the planet’s mantle and that it emerged onto the surface 10,000 years ago.

385.sword: Once every 1,000 years, the singing of a pure voice will rouse this Pokémon from its near- perpetual slumber. It wakes for only seven days.
385.shield: It’s believed that when this Pokémon wakes from its 1,000-year slumber, it will grant any wishes written on the notes attached to its head.

403.sword: This Pokémon generates electricity by contracting its muscles. Excited trembling is a sign that Shinx is generating a tremendous amount of electricity.
403.shield: Electricity makes this Pokémon’s fur glow. Shinx sends signals to others of its kind by shaking the tip of its tail while the tail tip is shining brightly.

404.sword: By joining its tail with that of another Luxio, this Pokémon can receive some of the other Luxio’s electricity and power up its own electric blasts.
404.shield: Upon encountering an opponent, this Pokémon prepares for battle by extending its claws, which can put out 1,000,000 volts of electricity.

405.sword: Luxray can see through solid objects. It will instantly spot prey trying to hide behind walls, even if the walls are thick.
405.shield: Seeing through solid objects uses up a lot of Luxray’s electricity, so the Pokémon sleeps for long periods of time to store up energy.

406.sword: The pollen it releases contains poison. If this Pokémon is raised on clean water, the poison’s toxicity is increased.
406.shield: This Pokémon is highly sensitive to temperature changes. When its bud starts to open, that means spring is right around the corner.

407.sword: After captivating opponents with its sweet scent, it lashes them with its thorny whips.
407.shield: The poison in its right hand is quick acting. The poison in its left hand is slow acting. Both are life threatening.

415.sword: The members of the trio spend all their time together. Each one has a slightly different taste in nectar.
415.shield: It ceaselessly gathers nectar from sunrise to sundown, all for the sake of Vespiquen and the swarm.

416.sword: It skillfully commands its grubs in battles with its enemies. The grubs are willing to risk their lives to defend Vespiquen.
416.shield: Vespiquen that give off more pheromones have larger swarms of Combee attendants.

420.sword: It nimbly dashes about to avoid getting pecked by bird Pokémon that would love to make off with its small, nutrient-rich storage ball.
420.shield: The deeper a Cherubi’s red, the more nutrients it has stockpiled in its body. And the sweeter and tastier its small ball!

421.sword: As a bud, it barely moves. It sits still, placidly waiting for sunlight to appear.
421.shield: Its folded petals are pretty tough. Bird Pokémon can peck at them all they want, and Cherrim won’t be bothered at all.

422.sword: This Pokémon’s habitat shapes its physique. According to some theories, life in warm ocean waters causes this variation to develop.
422.shield: Subjecting this Pokémon to a strong force causes it to secrete a strange purple fluid. Though harmless, the fluid is awfully sticky.

423.sword: Its search for food sometimes leads it onto land, where it leaves behind a sticky trail of slime as it passes through.
423.shield: The softness of its body helps disperse the force of impacts, so although its body is uncommonly squishy, it’s also surprisingly resilient.

425.sword: Perhaps seeking company, it approaches children. However, it often quickly runs away again when the children play too roughly with it.
425.shield: The gathering of many souls gave rise to this Pokémon. During humid seasons, they seem to appear in abundance.

426.sword: Some say this Pokémon is a collection of souls burdened with regrets, silently drifting through the dusk.
426.shield: It grabs people and Pokémon and carries them off somewhere. Where do they go? Nobody knows.

427.sword: If both of Buneary’s ears are rolled up, something is wrong with its body or mind. It’s a sure sign the Pokémon is in need of care.
427.shield: Buneary can attack by rolling up their ears and then striking with the force created by unrolling them. This attack becomes stronger with training.

428.sword: Lopunny is constantly monitoring its surroundings. If danger approaches, this Pokémon responds with superdestructive kicks.
428.shield: Once hot seasons are over, Lopunny’s coat will be replaced with fur that holds a lot of insulating air in preparation for colder weather.

434.sword: From its rear, it sprays a foul-smelling liquid at opponents. It aims for their faces, and it can hit them from over 16 feet away.
434.shield: If it lifts its tail and points its rear at you, beware. It’s about to spray you with a fluid stinky enough to make you faint.

435.sword: In its belly, it reserves stinky fluid that it shoots from its tail during battle. As this Pokémon’s diet varies, so does the stench of its fluid.
435.shield: It digs holes in the ground to make its nest. The stench of the fluid it lets fly from the tip of its tail is extremely potent.

436.sword: It appears in ancient ruins. The pattern on its body doesn’t come from any culture in the Galar region, so it remains shrouded in mystery.
436.shield: Polishing Bronzor to a shine makes its surface reflect the truth, according to common lore. Be that as it may, Bronzor hates being polished.

437.sword: Some believe it to be a deity that summons rain clouds. When angered, it lets out a warning cry that rings out like the tolling of a bell.
437.shield: Many scientists suspect that this Pokémon originated outside the Galar region, based on the patterns on its body.

438.sword: It expels both sweat and tears from its eyes. The sweat is a little salty, while the tears have a slight bitterness.
438.shield: This Pokémon lives in dry, rocky areas. As its green spheres dry out, their dull luster increases.

439.sword: It mimics everyone it sees, but it puts extra effort into copying the graceful dance steps of Mr. Rime as practice.
439.shield: It looks for a Mr. Rime that’s a good dancer and carefully copies the Mr. Rime’s steps like an apprentice.

440.sword: Mimicking Chansey, Happiny will place an egg- shaped stone in its belly pouch. Happiny will treasure this stone.
440.shield: Happiny’s willing to lend its precious round stone to those it’s friendly with, but if the stone isn’t returned, Happiny will cry and throw a tantrum.

442.sword: Exactly 108 spirits gathered to become this Pokémon. Apparently there are some ill-natured spirits in the mix.
442.shield: All Spiritomb’s mischief and misdeeds compelled a traveler to use a mysterious spell to bind Spiritomb to an odd keystone.

443.sword: Gible prefers to stay in narrow holes in the sides of caves heated by geothermal energy. This way, Gible can stay warm even during a blizzard.
443.shield: Gible attacks anything that moves, and it drags whatever it catches into the crevice that is its lair. Despite the big mouth, Gible’s stomach is small.

444.sword: This Pokémon emits ultrasonic waves from a protrusion on either side of its head to probe pitch-dark caves.
444.shield: Jewels are buried in the caves these Pokémon nest in, but you’ll be torn apart by claws and fangs the moment you enter one of these caves.

445.sword: Garchomp makes its home in volcanic mountains. It flies through the sky as fast as a jet airplane, hunting down as much prey as it can.
445.shield: Garchomp is fast both underground and above. It can bring down prey and return to its den before its body has chilled from being outside.

446.sword: Stuffing itself with vast amounts of food is its only concern. Whether the food is rotten or fresh, yummy or tasteless—it does not care.
446.shield: It stores food beneath its fur. It might share just one bite, but only if it really trusts you.

447.sword: It’s exceedingly energetic, with enough stamina to keep running all through the night. Taking it for walks can be a challenging experience.
447.shield: It can use waves called auras to gauge how others are feeling. These same waves can also tell this Pokémon about the state of the environment.

448.sword: It controls waves known as auras, which are powerful enough to pulverize huge rocks. It uses these waves to take down its prey.
448.shield: It can tell what people are thinking. Only Trainers who have justice in their hearts can earn this Pokémon’s trust.

449.sword: It moves through the sands with its mouth open, swallowing sand along with its prey. It gets rid of the sand by spouting it from its nose.
449.shield: This Pokémon is active during the day and passes the cold desert nights burrowed snugly into the sand.

450.sword: Stones can get stuck in the ports on their bodies. Dwebble help dislodge such stones, so Hippowdon look after these Pokémon.
450.shield: When roused to violence by its rage, it spews out the quantities of sand it has swallowed and whips up a sandstorm.

451.sword: After burrowing into the sand, it waits patiently for prey to come near. This Pokémon and Sizzlipede share common descent.
451.shield: It attacks using the claws on its tail. Once locked in its grip, its prey is unable to move as this Pokémon’s poison seeps in.

452.sword: Its poison is potent, but it rarely sees use. This Pokémon prefers to use physical force instead, going on rampages with its car-crushing strength.
452.shield: It’s so vicious that it’s called the Sand Demon. Yet when confronted by Hippowdon, Drapion keeps a low profile and will never pick a fight.

453.sword: It makes frightening noises with its poison-filled cheek sacs. When opponents flinch, Croagunk hits them with a poison jab.
453.shield: Once diluted, its poison becomes medicinal. This Pokémon came into popularity after a pharmaceutical company chose it as a mascot.

454.sword: It bounces toward opponents and gouges them with poisonous claws. No more than a scratch is needed to knock out its adversaries.
454.shield: It booms out a victory croak when its prey goes down in defeat. This Pokémon and Seismitoad are related species.

458.sword: Mantyke living in Galar seem to be somewhat sluggish. The colder waters of the seas in this region may be the cause.
458.shield: It swims along with a school of Remoraid, and they’ll all fight together to repel attackers.

459.sword: It lives on snowy mountains. It sinks its legs into the snow to absorb water and keep its own temperature down.
459.shield: The berries that grow around its belly are like ice pops. Galarian Darumaka absolutely love these berries.

460.sword: If it sees any packs of Darumaka going after Snover, it chases them off, swinging its sizable arms like hammers.
460.shield: This Pokémon is known to bring blizzards. A shake of its massive body is enough to cause whiteout conditions.

461.sword: They attack their quarry in packs. Prey as large as Mamoswine easily fall to the teamwork of a group of Weavile.
461.shield: With its claws, it leaves behind signs for its friends to find. The number of distinct signs is said to be over 500.

462.sword: Some say that Magnezone receives signals from space via the antenna on its head and that it’s being controlled by some mysterious being.
462.shield: It’s thought that a special magnetic field changed the molecular structure of this Pokémon’s body, and that’s what caused the Pokémon’s evolution.

463.sword: Lickilicky’s strange tongue can stretch to many times the length of its body. No one has figured out how Lickilicky’s tongue can stretch so far.
463.shield: Lickilicky can do just about anything with its tongue, which is as dexterous as the human hand. In contrast, Lickilicky’s use of its fingers is clumsy.

464.sword: It can load up to three projectiles per arm into the holes in its hands. What launches out of those holes could be either rocks or Roggenrola.
464.shield: It relies on its carapace to deflect incoming attacks and throw its enemy off balance. As soon as that happens, it drives its drill into the foe.

465.sword: Tangrowth has two arms that it can extend as it pleases. Recent research has shown that these arms are, in fact, bundles of vines.
465.shield: Vine growth is accelerated for Tangrowth living in warm climates. If the vines grow long, Tangrowth shortens them by tearing parts of them off.

466.sword: The amount of electrical energy this Pokémon produces is proportional to the rate of its pulse. The voltage jumps while Electivire is battling.
466.shield: In terms of electrical-energy output, Electivire is one of the best among all Electric Pokémon. It discharges high-voltage currents from its tails.

467.sword: When Magmortar inhales deeply, the fire burning in its belly intensifies, rising in temperature to over 3,600 degrees Fahrenheit.
467.shield: Living in the crater of a volcano has caused this Pokémon’s body to resemble its environment— it has an organ similar to a magma chamber.

468.sword: These Pokémon are never seen anywhere near conflict or turmoil. In recent times, they’ve hardly been seen at all.
468.shield: Known as a bringer of blessings, it’s been depicted on good-luck charms since ancient times.

470.sword: Galarians favor the distinctive aroma that drifts from this Pokémon’s leaves. There’s a popular perfume made using that scent.
470.shield: This Pokémon’s tail is blade sharp, with a fantastic cutting edge that can slice right though large trees.

471.sword: Any who become captivated by the beauty of the snowfall that Glaceon creates will be frozen before they know it.
471.shield: The coldness emanating from Glaceon causes powdery snow to form, making it quite a popular Pokémon at ski resorts.

473.sword: This Pokémon can be spotted in wall paintings from as far back as 10,000 years ago. For a while, it was thought to have gone extinct.
473.shield: It looks strong, and that’s exactly what it is. As the weather grows colder, its ice tusks grow longer, thicker, and more impressive.

474.sword: Porygon-Z had a program installed to allow it to move between dimensions, but the program also caused instability in Porygon-Z’s behavior.
474.shield: Some say an additional program made this Pokémon evolve, but even academics can’t agree on whether Porygon-Z is really an evolution.

475.sword: True to its honorable-warrior image, it uses the blades on its elbows only in defense of something or someone.
475.shield: Sharply attuned to others’ wishes for help, this Pokémon seeks out those in need and aids them in battle.

477.sword: At the bidding of transmissions from the spirit world, it steals people and Pokémon away. No one knows whether it has a will of its own.
477.shield: With the mouth on its belly, Dusknoir swallows its target whole. The soul is the only thing eaten— Dusknoir disgorges the body before departing.

478.sword: After a woman met her end on a snowy mountain, her regrets lingered on. From them, this Pokémon was born. Its favorite food is frozen souls.
478.shield: It spits out cold air of nearly −60 degrees Fahrenheit to freeze its quarry. It brings frozen prey back to its lair and neatly lines them up.

479.sword: One boy’s invention led to the development of many different machines that take advantage of Rotom’s unique capabilities.
479.shield: With a body made of plasma, it can inhabit all sorts of machines. It loves to surprise others.

486.sword: All over the world, there are legends that tell of Regigigas creating other Pokémon in its own image.
486.shield: It’s said that Regigigas created other Pokémon from many different materials before it moved the continents to where they are today.

506.sword: This Pokémon is courageous but also cautious. It uses the soft fur covering its face to collect information about its surroundings.
506.shield: This Pokémon is far brighter than the average child, and Lillipup won’t forget the love it receives or any abuse it suffers.

507.sword: Herdier is a very smart and friendly Pokémon. So much so that there’s a theory that Herdier was the first Pokémon to partner with people.
507.shield: The black fur that covers this Pokémon’s body is dense and springy. Even sharp fangs bounce right off.

508.sword: These Pokémon seem to enjoy living with humans. Even a Stoutland caught in the wild will warm up to people in about three days.
508.shield: Stoutland is immensely proud of its impressive moustache. It’s said that moustache length is what determines social standing among this species.

509.sword: It steals things from people just to amuse itself with their frustration. A rivalry exists between this Pokémon and Nickit.
509.shield: Opponents that get drawn in by its adorable behavior come away with stinging scratches from its claws and stinging pride from its laughter.

510.sword: Don’t be fooled by its gorgeous fur and elegant figure. This is a moody and vicious Pokémon.
510.shield: This stealthy Pokémon sneaks up behind prey without making any sound at all. It competes with Thievul for territory.

517.sword: Late at night, it appears beside people’s pillows. As it feeds on dreams, the patterns on its body give off a faint glow.
517.shield: It eats dreams and releases mist. The mist is pink when it’s eating a good dream, and black when it’s eating a nightmare.

518.sword: When dark mists emanate from its body, don’t get too near. If you do, your nightmares will become reality.
518.shield: It drowses and dreams all the time. It’s best to leave it be if it’s just woken up, as it’s a terrible grump when freshly roused from sleep.

519.sword: Where people go, these Pokémon follow. If you’re scattering food for them, be careful— several hundred of them can gather at once.
519.shield: It’s forgetful and not very bright, but many Trainers love it anyway for its friendliness and sincerity.

520.sword: It can fly moderately quickly. No matter how far it travels, it can always find its way back to its master and its nest.
520.shield: These bright Pokémon have acute memories. Apparently delivery workers often choose them as their partners.

521.sword: Unfezant are exceptional fliers. The females are known for their stamina, while the males outclass them in terms of speed.
521.shield: This Pokémon is intelligent and intensely proud. People will sit up and take notice if you become the Trainer of one.

524.sword: It’s as hard as steel, but apparently a long soak in water will cause it to soften a bit.
524.shield: When it detects a noise, it starts to move. The energy core inside it makes this Pokémon slightly warm to the touch.

525.sword: If you see its orange crystals start to glow, be wary. It’s about to fire off bursts of energy.
525.shield: It relies on sound in order to monitor what’s in its vicinity. When angered, it will attack without ever changing the direction it’s facing.

526.sword: This hardy Pokémon can often be found on construction sites and in mines, working alongside people and Copperajah.
526.shield: Although its energy blasts can blow away a dump truck, they have a limitation— they can only be fired when the sun is out.

527.sword: While inside a cave, if you look up and see lots of heart-shaped marks lining the walls, it’s evidence that Woobat live there.
527.shield: It emits ultrasonic waves as it flutters about, searching for its prey—bug Pokémon.

528.sword: Emitting powerful sound waves tires it out. Afterward, it won’t be able to fly for a little while.
528.shield: The auspicious shape of this Pokémon’s nose apparently led some regions to consider Swoobat a symbol of good luck.

529.sword: It brings its claws together and whirls around at high speed before rushing toward its prey.
529.shield: It’s a digger, using its claws to burrow through the ground. It causes damage to vegetable crops, so many farmers have little love for it.

530.sword: It’s not uncommon for tunnels that appear to have formed naturally to actually be a result of Excadrill’s rampant digging.
530.shield: Known as the Drill King, this Pokémon can tunnel through the terrain at speeds of over 90 mph.

531.sword: Audino’s sense of hearing is superb. Not even a pebble rolling along over a mile away will escape Audino’s ears.
531.shield: This Pokémon has a kind heart. By touching with its feelers, Audino can gauge other creatures’ feelings and physical conditions.

532.sword: It loves helping out with construction projects. It loves it so much that if rain causes work to halt, it swings its log around and throws a tantrum.
532.shield: Timburr that have started carrying logs that are about three times their size are nearly ready to evolve.

533.sword: It shows off its muscles to Machoke and other Gurdurr. If it fails to measure up to the other Pokémon, it lies low for a little while.
